itemWritingReference.title: NBME Item-Writing Guide for Constructed-Response and Multiple-Choice Items

difficultyRubric.axes: Level describes the scope of engineering judgment; difficultyBand describes challenge relative to other items at that same level.

levels.junior: An isolated language, browser, or standard framework contract with one local owner and an immediately observable consequence. A paired API that forms one contract—such as input/output, model prop/event, native form behavior, or provider scope—can remain junior.
levels.mid: A lifecycle, asynchronous, layout, render, or ownership boundary that requires connecting at least two independently failing mechanisms in an application context; recognizing two parts of one standard API is not enough by itself.
levels.senior: A cross-instance, cross-request, hydration, rendering-system, or performance-architecture decision spanning multiple lifetimes or operational consequences. Code-output items may instead require Promise adoption, error recovery, and cleanup/pass-through behavior across at least three interacting boundaries.

bands.foundation: Baseline knowledge expected at the declared level, with the governing contract explicit in the scenario.
bands.core: Root-cause selection across at least two realistic constraints or competing remedies at the declared level.
bands.stretch: A subtle ordering, version, ownership, or multi-constraint distinction near the upper edge of the declared level.

difficultyRubric.levelAllocationRule: The 60-item blueprint contains exactly 20 junior, 20 mid, and 20 senior items. Compare the full corpus when assigning levels; if an item cannot defensibly fit its cohort under the scope definitions, flag it instead of forcing the quota.
difficultyRubric.crossLevelRule: Bands are not absolute across levels; a senior foundation item can be more direct than a mid stretch item while still testing senior scope.
difficultyRubric.bandAllocationRule: After assigning level, rank items comparatively within each 20-item level cohort: exactly 5 foundation, 10 core, and 5 stretch. Never change a level merely to satisfy a band quota.
difficultyRubric.blindReviewRule: A blind reviewer must apply this rubric and comparative allocation without seeing the authored level, band, correct option, rationales, or provenance.
